key_insight: The paper argues that explainable AI in medicine should be grounded in philosophy of science, especially around causality, trust, and what counts as an adequate explanation.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI to be useful and trustworthy, its explanations must fit the needs of different healthcare stakeholders, not just be technically interpretable.
method: Critical review at the intersection of philosophy of science and explainable AI
Synthesizes accounts of explanation in the health sciences
Identifies three analysis axes: causality, trust, and explanatory adequacy
evidence_signal: This is a conceptual review based on existing philosophical and XAI literature, rather than a new empirical dataset or model evaluation.
watch_item: A key challenge is that explanation standards may differ across clinicians, patients, and developers, making a one-size-fits-all XAI design unlikely.
paper_title: Scientific Explanations in Health Sciences: Causality, Trust, and Epistemic Adequacy
